judge: Dana — data-loss and save-state adversary (lost a 40k-word draft to a sync conflict; reads every save state, dialog, sign-out and reload path with suspicion)
first_five_minutes:
Connected mode, the way it will actually land tomorrow. Cassy opens the link and gets /login: "WELCOME HOME, CASSANDRA · Your private workspace · Sign in to pick up where you left off" beside a daily quote and "A little more room to be the author." It is warm and it is hers. She signs in and lands on "Welcome home, Cassandra." with a locked-padlock "Private workspace" chip, a quote, the inspiration shelf, a desk card, and a three-step "Start with one small thing." Counts read "—" for a beat and then fill in. Nothing is shouting at her. This is the best part of the app and it does its job.

Her first click is almost certainly "Open your books" (step 01) or the Universe card, because the deck she has been shown is about her books. She opens Assassin's Refusal. The right-hand panel is the biggest thing on the page: "Let Kira get to know this book." A file picker, one checkbox — "I have permission to upload this manuscript and have Kira's AI services analyze it privately for book knowledge" — and one gold button, "Upload & let Kira read" (components/kira/connected-book-detail.tsx:119).

This is the moment I care about, and it is the moment the app is least honest with her. That one click does three irreversible things at once: it writes her manuscript file into permanent private storage, it chops the full text into stored passages, and it starts shipping those passages out of Supabase to google/gemini-3.8-flash and openai/text-embedding-3-small through Vercel AI Gateway (docs/manuscript-foundation.md:64 says so plainly; the checkbox does not). Then she will look for the way to take it back — because every author who has ever uploaded a manuscript looks for that — and there is no delete control on the page, no delete endpoint in app/api/manuscripts/*, and supabase/migrations/202609190001_manuscript_intelligence.sql:473 installs a restrictive policy that makes deleting the stored object impossible for any authenticated user, including her. "Manuscript history · 2 versions" will accumulate forever.

If instead she starts at the desk, minute four looks like this: she types a real idea into "Your idea", sees the reassuring "Not saved yet · Kept while you explore. Save before reloading or signing out.", then alt-tabs to find the promo date in her email. On return, the window focus handler fires a background refresh (lib/db/demo-store.tsx:468, components/kira/library-provider.tsx:56). If her session has lapsed — the ordinary case — the 401 path at lib/db/demo-store.tsx:133-141 and library-provider.tsx:33-34 wipes every in-memory draft and hard-navigates her to /login. She gets no dialog, no "copy your text first", no recovery. The words are simply gone, and the thing that took them is the app noticing she came back.

scores.verdict: Consent is asked for clearly at the moment of upload, and role limits are explained without condescension — but the two controls that would make consent real are missing: she cannot delete her manuscript (the SQL forbids it outright), and she cannot separate 'store my file' from 'send my prose to an external model'. One button does both, permanently.

top_findings.title: A background refresh on window focus destroys every unsaved draft and hard-navigates to /login
top_findings.problem: Three code paths respond to 401 (and GET 403) by wiping in-memory scratchpads and calling window.location.replace("/login"): lib/db/demo-store.tsx:133-141, components/kira/library-provider.tsx:33-34, components/kira/studio-page.tsx:80-84 and 123-127. All three are reachable from background refreshes that fire on every window focus (demo-store.tsx:468-470, library-provider.tsx:56-57). So the ordinary sequence — type a desk brief or a Raven question, tab away, session lapses, tab back — silently deletes her words. Worse, clearPrivateScratchpads()/emptyWorkspace() run *before* the navigation, so if the browser's beforeunload prompt appears and she chooses 'Stay', she is left sitting on an emptied form with nothing to copy.
top_findings.proposed_change: Replace the clear-and-redirect with a blocking 'Your session ended' dialog that renders every non-empty scratchpad read-only with a Copy button and a 'Sign in again' action; clear state only after she confirms. Never clear scratchpads before a navigation that can be cancelled.

top_findings.title: A manuscript can be uploaded but never deleted, by her or by anyone using the app
top_findings.problem: There is no delete control in components/kira/connected-book-detail.tsx, no DELETE handler under app/api/manuscripts/*, and the migration installs a restrictive policy — kira_manuscript_no_delete — that blocks deletion of objects in the kira-manuscripts bucket for every authenticated role. Related tables use `on delete restrict` and the manuscripts table comment calls versions 'immutable'. Nothing in the UI tells her this before she clicks 'Upload & let Kira read'. For an unpublished novel this is the most consequential property of the feature and it is invisible.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add a per-version 'Remove this version' control (owner/editor, typed-title confirm) plus 'Download my original file'; back it with a DELETE route and a migration replacing the blanket no-delete policy with one scoped to private.can_edit_author(m.author_id), cascading that manuscript's chunks and knowledge rows. If permanence is a deliberate product choice, state it on the upload panel instead.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Michael must decide whether manuscript versions are deliberately immutable-forever (an audit/rights stance) or deletable by the author. The disclosure copy is code either way; the policy change is not.

top_findings.title: The upload consent does not say her prose is sent to Google and OpenAI
top_findings.problem: The checkbox reads '…have Kira's AI services analyze it privately for book knowledge.' docs/manuscript-foundation.md:64 states the passages go through Vercel AI Gateway to google/gemini-3.8-flash and openai/text-embedding-3-small and that this 'is not processing confined entirely to Supabase or the user's device'. The honest sentence is in a doc she will never open; the vague one is attached to the irreversible button. connected-library.tsx:67 reinforces the wrong impression with 'Private to your workspace.'
top_findings.proposed_change: Append to the existing label (after the pinned '/I have permission to upload/' prefix): 'Passages are sent to third-party AI models (Google Gemini, OpenAI embeddings) through Vercel AI Gateway. Your file and its saved passages stay in this workspace.' Amend connected-library.tsx:67 to match.

top_findings.title: The Edit dialog silently discards a rewritten brief on Escape
top_findings.problem: `draft` is a single local state seeded by setDraft(approval.draft) every time Edit opens (line 101), and the Dialog's onOpenChange (line 162-163) closes with no unsaved-changes check. Escape or a backdrop click closes the dialog; reopening Edit overwrites her rewrite with the stored version. The text is also invisible to hasPrivateDrafts() (demo-store.tsx:63-72), so beforeunload and the sign-out confirmation do not protect it either. Up to 10,000 characters, no warning, no undo.
top_findings.proposed_change: Key the draft per approval id+version, do not re-seed over a newer local edit, add an unsaved-changes confirm to onOpenChange, and register these edits in hasPrivateDrafts() so reload and sign-out guards see them.

top_findings.title: 'Could not be saved' can be a lie that costs her a duplicate — no idempotency on create/teach
top_findings.problem: The `create` and `teach` commands take no client-supplied id, unlike /api/studio and /api/plans which both accept one. If the row commits and the response is lost, demo-store.perform() throws, manual-review-form.tsx:99 shows 'Your idea could not be saved. Your text is still here; please try again.', and her retry writes a second brief. The message is reassuring and wrong about the outcome.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add a required `id: z.uuid()` to both commands, insert idempotently on it in the connected repository, and have createManualReview/teachRaven generate the id once and reuse it across retries.

top_findings.title: The corrupt-storage error tells her to export data that cannot be exported, then overwrites it
top_findings.problem: When parseWorkspace throws, the message is 'Browser storage is unavailable or contains an incompatible workspace. Export any existing data before resetting.' But exportWorkspace() (line 410) serializes the in-memory snapshot — which is the seeded fallback, not the unreadable localStorage value — and the very next successful save calls saveLocal() and overwrites the old value for good. The instruction is impossible to follow and the data is destroyed by the next click.
top_findings.proposed_change: Stash the raw unparseable string, offer 'Download the unreadable workspace file' and 'Start a fresh demo workspace', and block saveLocal() from overwriting until she picks one.

top_findings.title: The two draft-discarding dialogs make the destructive choice the primary button
top_findings.problem: 'Sign out and discard drafts' uses the default (gold, primary) variant while 'Keep working' is an outline; studio-page.tsx:206 repeats it with 'Discard draft and start fresh'. The app already gets this right elsewhere — settings-page.tsx:175-179 and access-page.tsx:157-158 both use variant="destructive" for the destructive action. The inconsistency lands precisely on the two dialogs that throw work away.
top_findings.proposed_change: Swap the variants in both dialogs: destructive for the discard action, default for the keep action. Focus already defaults to the safe button; keep that.

top_findings.title: Save failures are reported in 11px (10px on phones) corner text with a check-mark icon
top_findings.problem: Every workspace save failure surfaces only through the toast in app-shell.tsx:398-414, styled at 11px (globals.css:1154) and 10px at mobile widths (globals.css:2628), and app-shell.tsx:403 renders the same <Check/> icon for errors as for successes. A failed save looks, at a glance, exactly like a successful one.
top_findings.proposed_change: Raise toast text to 14px at all widths, give .toast-error an alert icon and distinct weight, and add aria-atomic="true" to the toast container.

top_findings.title: The global error screen tells connected users something false about where their work is
top_findings.problem: 'Your locally saved decisions are still in your browser.' is hardcoded and shown in both modes. In connected mode her decisions are in Supabase, not the browser, and the screen says nothing about whether anything she had typed survived. There is also no route out except 'Try again'.
top_findings.proposed_change: Mode-accurate copy that separates saved records ('safe — in your account' / 'safe — in this browser') from unsaved typing ('may not have survived; check before retyping'), plus a 'Back to Mission Control' link.

top_findings.title: The export omits more than it admits, and nothing can be imported back
top_findings.problem: exportWorkspace() (demo-store.tsx:410-424) serializes only approvals, feedback, dismissed, recommendations and last_run_at. Manuscripts, extracted book knowledge and marketing plans are silently absent; the copy names only 'Ask Raven answers and account connections' as excluded. There is no importer anywhere in the tree, yet the reset dialog at settings-page.tsx:171 offers 'Export your workspace first if you want to keep it.'
top_findings.proposed_change: Complete the exclusion list, and either add a demo-mode importer (file picker → workspaceSchema.parse → saveLocal) or change the reset dialog to say the file is a records copy that cannot be loaded back.

top_findings.title: 'The minions are working. Go write.' asserts background work that does not exist
top_findings.problem: Shown in the demo desk empty state and again at mission-control.tsx:94. Nothing is running; AGENTS.md forbids fake autonomous agent status. It is also the only line in the app that talks down to her, in an app whose whole voice is 'you are the expert'.
top_findings.proposed_change: 'Nothing is waiting on you right now. Go write.' in both places. No e2e test pins this string.

what_works: The three-way draft warning at manual-review-form.tsx:228, studio-page.tsx:186 and learn-page.tsx:175 is the best save-state copy I have read in a product like this: it names the exact hazards (reloading, closing the tab, signing out) instead of saying 'unsaved changes'. Keep the wording, and extend the same treatment to the Edit dialog and the book-details form rather than diluting it.

clearScratchpad(submitted) at demo-store.tsx:250-254 with the comment 'A completed save must never erase words entered after that submission' — a real race condition someone thought about and closed. Do not refactor it away.

WorkspaceProvider is keyed on `${mode}:${viewerEmail}` (demo-store.tsx:443) so a different signed-in account cannot inherit the previous person's private notes. Same pattern in LibraryProvider (library-provider.tsx:65).

Optimistic concurrency done properly: `version` on decide (api/workspace/route.ts:28), `expectedUpdatedAt` on book metadata (connected-library.tsx:31), `expected` on plans, and the changedSinceOpening guard at approval-card.tsx:41 with the 'This brief changed while you were reviewing it' alert at line 210. This is the part of the app that would have saved my 40k words.

The sign-out confirmation exists at all (app-shell.tsx:415-429), defaults focus to 'Keep working', and completeSignOut only clears scratchpads after the server confirms a real logout — with an honest failure message at line 270 ('Your unfinished work is still here').

Background manuscript reading is genuinely well-handled: durable progress, a real pause control, 'Completed passages stay saved', a stalled-job detector (connected-book-detail.tsx:75), and error copy that distinguishes 'your upload is saved, retry the reading' from 'the upload did not finish, select the same file'. Do not simplify these messages.

Spoiler gating defaults to off and is stated numerically — book-knowledge.tsx:89 shows 'N findings with potential spoilers are hidden', and the manuscript search requires a separate opt-in checkbox before any excerpt appears (connected-book-detail.tsx:135).

Citation discipline: every extracted finding links to the exact passage, the panel says findings whose quotations cannot be matched are omitted, and 'Interpretation · verify with source' is labelled distinctly from 'Manuscript-supported' (book-knowledge.tsx:102).

Destructive-action styling is already correct in settings-page.tsx:175-179 (Reset demo) and access-page.tsx:157-158 (Remove access) — use those two as the template when fixing the sign-out and studio dialogs.

Focus management is consistently thought through: error paragraphs are focusable with role=alert and get focus on failure (manual-review-form.tsx:83, learn-page.tsx:94), dialogs restore focus to their trigger or a sensible fallback (approval-card.tsx:170-175), and the permission notice returns focus to main after a successful retry (workspace-permission-notice.tsx:9-14).
